neighbours.label: musical performance and instrument technique (playing, phrasing, tone on an instrument or voice); parallel technique talk in non-musical crafts stays low
fire: A good cellist keeps the bow straight and lets the arm carry the weight.
On the flute, breath support decides how steady each long note sounds.
The pianist used the soft pedal to shade the quiet middle passage.
Beginners on the trumpet should practise long tones every morning.
Her violin tone grew richer once she relaxed her left hand.
The drummer kept a light touch on the hi-hat during the ballad.
When singing high notes, open the throat and keep the jaw loose.
The guitarist bent the string slowly to reach the note in tune.
quiet: A good carpenter keeps the saw straight and lets the arm carry the weight.
On the treadmill, steady breathing decides how long each run lasts.
The mechanic used a torque wrench to tighten the wheel nuts.
Beginners at the gym should practise squats every morning.
Her handwriting grew neater once she relaxed her grip on the pen.
The cook kept a low flame under the pan while the sauce reduced.
When lifting heavy boxes, bend the knees and keep the back straight.
The plumber turned the valve slowly to stop the leak.
